title: Germany launches its own fusion milestone program
summary: Germany’s Federal Agency for Breakthrough Innovation (SPRIND) has established a milestone-based fusion program on behalf of the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology, and Space (BMFTR) and as part of the government’s High-Tech Agenda Germany (HTAD). The initiative is designed to help the HTAD in its efforts to use technology-specific roadmaps and flagship programs to strengthen Germany’s high-performing technology innovation and to speed the conversion of tech research into practical applications. Through the new Milestone Program, the German government intends to provide financial support to fusion companies—particularly start-ups—to advance fusion technology development. The funds will be awarded via a competitive process.

title: CoP webinar lays out timeline of RIPB policy
summary: The American Nuclear Society’s Risk-informed, Performance-based Principles and Policy Committee (RP3C) recently held another presentation in its monthly Community of Practice (CoP) series. Former RP3C chair N. Prasad Kadambi opened the meeting with brief introductory remarks about the RP3C, the value of risk-informed, performance-based (RIPB) techniques, and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission’s current interest in and work on the field. After these remarks, Kadambi introduced this month’s speaker: Steven Krahn, a professor of the practice of nuclear environmental engineering at Vanderbilt University and chair of the RP3C committee. Krahn’s presentation was titled “The Evolution of the Understanding of Nuclear Reactor Risk and Risk-Informed, Performance-Based Policy in the U.S.”

title: Westinghouse moves forward on Polish, Dutch power plant projects
summary: Westinghouse continues to make progress on building the first nuclear power plant in Poland, having begun the long-lead-item procurement process and signed conditional purchase orders for the first of three planned AP1000 units. The company also announced recently that it will be partnering with Hyundai Engineering & Construction on the front-end engineering design (FEED) phase of a project to deploy two large-scale reactors in the Netherlands.

title: Bangladesh’s Rooppur-1 Nuclear Plant Achieves First Criticality
summary: Unit 1 at the Rooppur nuclear power station being built by Russia in Bangladesh has achieved criticality with grid connection expected by the end of November. The 1,080-MW VVER V-523 pressurised water reactor unit, construction of which began in 2017, achieved first criticality at 15:34 on 11 October. First criticality is the milestone moment when a nuclear reactor achieves a self-sustaining, controlled chain reaction for the very first time. Rooppur, Bangladesh’s most expensive infrastructure facility, has considerable backing from Russia. Moscow is financing $11.9bn (€10.6bn) in state loans for the project, which has been estimated to cost up to $12.8bn.
